extracted.intended_audience: journalists, newspaper editors, news agencies, media organisations, and policymakers in India
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and codifies the Press Council of India’s norms, procedural rules, advisories and adjudication principles for print (and related) media between April 1, 2022 and March 31, 2023. Useful for journalists, editors, media organisations and regulators in India.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objects of the Press Council (Section 13)
rubrics_metrics.description: The objects of the Press Council of India as embodied in Section 13 of the Act are to preserve the freedom of the Press and to maintain and improve the standards of newspapers and news agencies in India.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Act also confers an advisory role: the Council may, suo-motu or on reference by Government, undertake studies and express opinions on any bill, law or other matters concerning the Press and convey its opinion to the Government or persons concerned. It may take cognizance in matters of public importance and constitute Special Committees for on-the-spot inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of Conduct / Norms of Journalistic Conduct (purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: To build up a code of conduct for newspapers, news agencies and journalists in accordance with high professional standards; to help and guide the print media in maintaining and improving the professional standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Council publishes 'Norms of Journalistic Conduct' (2022 edition released Nov 16, 2022) updated based on adjudications. The Norms are used as the baseline for advisories and adjudications (e.g., on paid news, reporting of sex workers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain independence of newspapers, news agencies and journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Help newspapers and news agencies to maintain their independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Council’s functions is to foster an environment where editorial and organisational independence are preserved; concerns such as concentration of ownership that impair independence should be monitored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain high standards of public taste and foster rights and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure on the part of newspapers, news agencies and journalists the maintenance of high standards of public taste and foster a due sense of both rights and responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to judge unethical writings, vulgar/obscene advertisements, sensationalism, and material that incites communal tensions; violations may trigger adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid paid news
rubrics_metrics.description: Paid news is a recognised malady; print media should follow the Norms of Journalistic Conduct (2022) on Paid News, especially during elections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory issued to print media to observe these Norms during elections; paid-for coverage can lead to adjudication and sanctions. The Council also issues advisories to reinforce compliance during electoral periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid fake news; institute fact-checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations to tackle fake news: (i) there must be a single organisation specially to tackle fake news; (ii) there should be a 'Fact Checking mechanism' within the news media organisation itself before publishing any news article; (iii) government awareness creation; (iv) bring fake news on electronic platforms under PCI until Media Council formed; (v) implement mechanism to identify generation/source point of fake news; (vi) include media studies in academic curriculum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are Council recommendations forwarded to the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting (inputs sent 08.12.2022). They function as operational and policy-level standards for news organisations and government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sensationalism, obscene/vulgar advertisements and communal-inciting content
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council identifies paid news, fake news, sensationalism, and obscene/vulgar advertisements, as well as news that incites communal tensions, as issues plaguing journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such content is liable to adjudication. The Council has taken suo-motu cognizance and issued censure or directions in multiple cases involving vulgar/obscene or misleading advertisements and communal/derogatory language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting on sex workers: protect identity and avoid voyeuristic images
rubrics_metrics.description: The media to take utmost care not to reveal the identities of sex workers, during arrest, raid and rescue operations, whether as victims or accused and not to publish or telecast any photos that would result in disclosure of such identities. The Section 354C IPC (voyeurism) should be strictly adhered to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This norm was incorporated into the Norms of Journalistic Conduct, 2022 and an advisory was issued. It arose from a Supreme Court reference and is explicitly enforced in adjudications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect physical safety of journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Any injury caused to a journalist while he is reporting is a cause for concern even if the journalist is not targeted on purpose; the police should be cautious while using water cannons or other methods during protests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Chairperson has taken suo-motu cognizance of incidents of attacks on journalists and notified concerned governments condemning such incidents; Council can recommend protective measures and record principles in adjudications.

rubrics_metrics.name: No payments/bribes from officials to journalists for coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Officials holding important positions should not give any amount to journalists for giving coverage to programmes of national importance like republic day, independence day, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjudications record censure/warnings where bribery or inducement for favourable coverage is alleged; this is treated as conduct undermining press independence and integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertiser verification: letterhead and PAN requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertisers should send their advertisements to the newspapers on their letterheads and for identity they should give their PAN card details to save prospective job aspirants from being deceived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recorded as an index principle in adjudications; the Council expects newspapers to verify advertisers' identity and to guard against fraudulent job-scam advertisements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press must spread brotherhood and avoid inflammatory communal content
rubrics_metrics.description: The press has to spread the message of brotherhood amongst people of all communities; it should desist from publishing inflammatory articles that can fan the flames of communalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjudications have censured publications for communal or hateful content; editors and newspapers are expected to promote unity in diversity rather than discord.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apologies must be genuine and not coerced
rubrics_metrics.description: Apology or expression of regret about an impugned publication targeting a particular community should not be done out of fear of mob/rioters; such an apology is not genuine and is an example of the worst kind of journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council distinguishes between voluntary, sincere apologies and those procured under duress; the latter do not absolve journalistic responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal editorial governance: editor–reporter interaction mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Every newspaper should have an internal mechanism by which there can be periodical interaction between editors and news reporters so that the importance of norms of Journalistic Conduct could be impressed upon them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a recommended organisational standard to inculcate ethics and professional norms across staff; compliance can be noted in adjudications and inspections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertisement screening machinery
rubrics_metrics.description: The press should have a machinery in place to scan properly all the advertisements which they receive and then segregate such advertisements which are not permissible as per the norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newspapers are expected to vet ads for legality and ethical compliance (e.g., obscene, misleading or fraudulent ads); failures have led to suo-motu cognizance and censure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors should not publish articles derogatory to a religion
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor holds the highest position in a newspaper and is responsible for selection of news. He should not write articles derogatory to a particular religion; such irresponsible behaviour is not expected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjudications have censured editors for derogatory pieces; editorial responsibility is emphasised both in Norms and in Council decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural standards for PCI inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: Inquiry proceedings are open to the general public; parties are required to present/furnish relevant evidence, oral or documentary and are allowed to be represented by lawyers/authorized representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inquiry Committees consider records and oral submissions, then place recommendations to the Council for final ratification. These procedural safeguards govern adjudication fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudicatory remedies and finality of decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Council is satisfied, after inquiry, that a newspaper/news agency has offended standards, the Council may warn, admonish or censure them or disapprove of their conduct. The decisions of the Council shall be final and shall not be questioned in any court of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctions include warning, admonition, censure, disapproval and public observations against authorities interfering with press freedom (Section 14). Decisions are intended to be authoritative and final under the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suo-motu cognizance for matters affecting press freedom or ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council may take suo-motu cognizance of incidents affecting press freedom or offending standards of journalistic ethics/public taste and constitute Committees to inquire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Chairperson has used suo-motu powers to address attacks on journalists, alleged obstruction of media access, obscene advertisements, and derogatory publications; such matters may result in censure or directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election reporting: follow ECI directions and avoid pre-result predictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory for print media to observe the direction laid in the ECI’s Advisory concerning prediction of results; advisory issued not to breach Section 126A of the Representation of People Act, 1951.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council also advised print media to follow Norms of Journalistic Conduct-2022 on Paid News for observance during elections; these are mandatory guidance points during electoral periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety guidelines for media persons covering natural disasters
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognising risks to life while covering natural disasters, the Council constituted a Sub-Committee to frame guidelines/SOP for the safety of media persons/reporters covering news amidst natural disaster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sub-committee formed (22.09.2022); report awaited. This reflects an organisational expectation to adopt SOPs to mitigate mortality/morbidity risks in disaster coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to include digital/electronic media in Press Council Act
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council recommended suggesting the Government make amendments in the Press Council Act itself incorporating electronic, digital and other media and that the Council's views may be obtained whenever such legislation is proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a policy/legislative standard to extend norms and oversight to new media formats; reflects Council’s view on coverage scope.
